title: Accessibility curvature law
dek: V824: spatial compression of reachable-state accessibility generates conformal, curvature-like scalar structure. Scalar/conformal sector only. Not tensor Einstein.
text:
Author: Aaron Spradlin. Program: Recoverability Geometry / Accessibility Branch. Version V824, 20 May 2026. The paper asks whether ordered-update recoverability systems naturally generate geometry-like structure. The strongest validated branch was accessibility geometry, not tensor transport.

G_{\mathrm{proxy}} = 2\alpha\,\Delta\log(A + \varepsilon),\quad A = \exp(C - \mu + \eta\,\mathrm{repair})

With accessibility potential φ = −α log(A+ε) and G_proxy = −2Δφ, the effective conformal factor is Ω = exp(φ), g_eff = Ω² g₀. Held-out R² ≈ 0.879 (mean), correlation ≈ 0.938; compressed operator R² ≈ 0.917; direct perturbation δG R² = 1.000; adversarial nulls next-best ≈ 0.

Supported vs failed branches

Supported: scalar/conformal accessibility-curvature law, Hamiltonian-like scalar closure, conformal geometry via Ω / g_eff.
Not supported: full tensor Einstein closure, ADM momentum constraints, conserved vector current, physical spacetime interpretation, local PDE evolution law for A. Tensor-branch attempts failed.

Recoverability pressure creates reachable-state density. Spatial compression of log accessibility generates curvature-like scalar structure.
